result: In 30 CFS vs 40 matched controls, CFS had low and unresponsive HRV, greater HR reactivity and prolonged HR recovery after cognitive challenge, and HRV predicted cognitive performance.
reason: Independent cohort showing reduced vagal HRV, same direction as finding; not among cited studies.

result: CFS patients (n=30) were significantly slower than 40 controls on cognitive tasks with no accuracy deficit, and lower HRV predicted poorer cognitive performance.
reason: Slowed processing/reaction time with spared accuracy replicates the speed deficit; small sample.

result: Six months after infectious mononucleosis, 9 of 36 adolescents with CFS (25%) vs 9 of 43 recovered controls (21%) had an abnormal standing orthostatic test, a non-significant difference.
reason: Measures orthostatic tolerance in the Katz cohort, not CFS incidence after mono; belongs with orthostatic/POTS findings.

result: Six months after infectious mononucleosis, 25% of adolescents with CFS vs 21% of recovered controls had an abnormal standing orthostatic test (not significant).
reason: Same measure (standing orthostatic test) in adolescents finds no excess over controls, against the Leone 2026 adolescent excess.

result: Of 25 people diagnosed with CFS 25 years earlier, 20 no longer reported the diagnosis, yet the remitted group was more impaired than controls on 21 of 23 outcomes and similar to persisting cases on 17.
reason: Long-term outcome adds that loss of diagnosis is not functional recovery; very small, self-reported.

result: In 68 Fukuda CFS vs 68 matched controls, resting LF-HRV was higher and parasympathetic HF markers lower (P=0.006), with altered BP variability; a combined index gave 77% sensitivity and 53% specificity.
reason: Independent cohort, same HRV measures, same direction; not among cited studies.

result: NK cytotoxic activity was lower in 65 CFS/ME than 21 controls at baseline, 6 and 12 months, with fewer CD56bright NK cells at baseline and 6 months and time-varying cytokine differences.
reason: Same Griffith group as cited Brenu 2011 (likely overlapping cohort); adds longitudinal stability rather than an independent replication.

result: In 47 adolescents with CFS re-tested 3-17 months later, baseline HR, BP, TPRI and LF/HF fell and tilt responses lessened alongside significant symptom and function improvement.
reason: Adds time course: autonomic markers improve with clinical improvement; no control group.

result: During graded tilt to 75 degrees in 16 CFS/POTS vs 20 controls, changes in cerebral blood flow velocity did not differ between groups and were unrelated to n-back scores.
reason: Same measure (TCD CBFV on tilt) finds no group difference; small CFS/POTS sample and velocity not volume flow.

result: CFS/POTS (n=16) had no supine n-back differences but lower accuracy and greater normalised reaction time than 20 controls at 45-75 degree tilt, especially on 2- to 4-back.
reason: Supports the claim that cognition worsens with upright posture; not a contradiction; independent of cited Medow 2014.
